# ja-ui — instructions for coding agents

ja-ui styles **plain semantic HTML5**. There is no `.btn`, no `.card`, no `.modal`. A
`<button>` is a button, `<dialog>` is the modal, `<details>` is the accordion, `[popover]`
is the dropdown. Read [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../ARCHITECTURE.md) before changing anything in
`src/styles/` — it is the contract, and it has the full class inventory and the
Bootstrap→native mapping table.

## Before you open the PR

```bash
npm ci
npm run build          # bundles, and runs lint:css at the end
npm run smoke          # drives the JS components in a real browser
npm run check:examples # drives the six example pages
npm run check:contrast # every token pair against WCAG AA
```

All four must pass. `npm run build` fails the moment a stylesheet is unlayered, uses
`!important`, uses a physical property, or reads a token that nothing declares — so a
green build is most of this document enforced mechanically. Fix the lint output; never
work around it.

## The ten rules that break most often

1. **The platform first.** Before writing anything, find the element that already does
   the job — check the mapping table in `ARCHITECTURE.md`. The normal fix is a few rules
   in an existing `src/styles/elements/*.css` file. A **new JS module is an admission
   that the platform has no answer** and must be justified in the PR body.
2. **No `!important`, anywhere.** It inverts cascade-layer order and would make this
   library beat the consumer's own CSS. If a rule is losing, it is in the wrong layer —
   move it, don't escalate it.
3. **Every rule lives in a layer.** `@layer ja.reset, ja.tokens, ja.elements, ja.variants,
   ja.components;` — bare elements and ARIA *state* selectors go in `ja.elements`, intent
   classes in `ja.variants`. Layer order sorts above specificity: that is how
   `<button type="submit" class="danger">` comes out red. Do not try to win a cascade
   fight with `:not()` chains or extra specificity.
4. **Variants only remap tokens.** A variant class sets custom properties and nothing
   else. Writing a raw `background:` in a variant rule is the single most common mistake:
   ```css
   button  { background: var(--ja-accent, var(--ja-surface)); }  /* element reads it */
   .danger { --ja-accent: var(--ja-danger); --ja-accent-fg: var(--ja-danger-fg); }
   .danger { background: red; }                                  /* ✗ never */
   ```
   The class inventory in `ARCHITECTURE.md` is **complete** — do not invent a new class.
   Colour (`.primary` … `.plain`), treatment (`.outline` `.soft` `.ghost`), size
   (`.sm` `.lg`). That's it.
5. **Every visual value is a token.** A colour, radius, shadow or duration literal inside
   an element file belongs in `src/styles/tokens.css` instead.
6. **Every colour is declared twice** — a plain fallback, then the `light-dark()` version.
   `light-dark()` is not a graceful no-op: on an unsupported browser it invalidates the
   whole declaration and the element gets *no* colour.
   ```css
   --ja-body-bg: #fffdf5;
   --ja-body-bg: light-dark(#fffdf5, #282c34);
   ```
7. **No element ships a margin.** Components own padding and internal `gap`; spacing
   between things belongs to the parent. There are no utility classes and no grid to fall
   back on — they were deliberately removed.
8. **ARIA state, never ARIA naming.** `[aria-expanded="true"]`, `[aria-current="page"]`,
   `[aria-selected="true"]` ✅. `[aria-label="Close"]` ✗ — that value is translated, so
   the style vanishes in French. Never use ARIA to pick a colour. Use `:user-invalid`,
   never `:invalid`.
9. **No wrapper elements.** Do not solve a problem by asking the consumer to add a
   grouping `<div>`, and do not introduce CSS that has to stay manually in sync with
   another rule. If a feature can only work that way, say so in the PR and leave it out.
10. **Zero runtime dependencies.** Dev dependencies are fine; nothing new may reach
    `dist/`. Accessibility is not a follow-up: visible focus, ≥44px targets, and motion
    respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Modern CSS only

Logical properties (`margin-inline`, not `margin-left`), `:has()`, `color-mix()`,
`light-dark()`, cascade layers, container queries. No floats, no clearfix, no vendor
prefixes, no physical `left`/`right`/`width` — the linter rejects them.

`ARCHITECTURE.md` has a feature-gating table: ship / guard-with-a-fallback / don't ship.
Anything in the middle column needs a real fallback — an unsupported `command` button is
**dead**, which is worse than not shipping it, so keep the JS click listener.

## If it needs JavaScript

Module in `src/js/`, exported from `src/index.js`, called from `src/js/autoinit.js`, typed
in `src/index.d.ts`, feature-detected with a fallback, and asserted in `tools/smoke.mjs`.

## Files you must not touch

- **`dist/`** — build output, regenerated by `npm run build`.
- **`docs/`** — gitignored build output for the published site. Never commit it, never
  hand-edit it. Edit the source in `site/`, `examples/` or `src/` instead.
- **`src/styles/generated/`** — does not exist any more. Edit the CSS directly.

Keep everything base-path agnostic: the site is served from `/<repo>/`, so no absolute
URLs (`/examples/…`) in the landing page, the examples or the stories.

## Commit and PR titles

The subject line **must start with one of these emoji**, then a space, then an imperative
lower-case subject with no trailing full stop. It records the semver bump, so a commit
without one cannot be versioned. One emoji per commit.

| Emoji | Meaning | Bump |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 🔥 | Breaking — removed or renamed a class, attribute, event, export or token | major |
| ✨ | New feature — a new component, variant or public API | minor |
| 🛠️ | Change — refactor, retune, perf, build or tooling | minor |
| 🐛 | Bug fix | patch |
| 📝 | Docs — README, CONTRIBUTING, stories, the site, comments | patch |

```
🐛 stop the command palette double-binding on re-init
✨ add a toast component
```

A 🔥 commit also needs a `BREAKING CHANGE:` paragraph in the body describing the
migration.

## What to put in the PR body

- Which native element or token you changed, and **why the platform didn't already do it**.
- The before/after in words — this library is reviewed by *looking* at it, so describe
  what visibly changes and on which example page or story.
- Anything you deliberately left out, and which rule above made you leave it out.

Add or update a story in `stories/` for anything visual.
